intro.text:
George Walker Bush (born July 6, 1946) is an American retired politician and businessman who served as the 43rd president of the United States from 2001 to 2009. A member of the Republican Party, he previously served as the 46th governor of Texas from 1995 to 2000. He is the eldest son of George H. W. Bush, the 41st president.
Born in New Haven, Connecticut, Bush graduated from Yale in 1968 with a bachelor in history. After service in the Texas Air National Guard, he graduated from Harvard Business School in 1975, before going back to Texas and founding his own oil company. Bush married Laura Welch, an elementary school librarian, in 1977. They had two children: Barbara and Jenna. In 1989, Bush bought out the Major League Baseball team Texas Rangers, becoming its co-owner. He ran for governor of Texas in 1994, winning by a clear margin. As governor, Bush sponsored tort reform legislation, increased funding for education, set higher standards for schools, and reformed the criminal justice system. He also helped make Texas the leading producer of wind-generated electricity in the United States. In the 2000 presidential election, he defeated Democratic incumbent vice president Al Gore...
